_meta.method: Every entry was checked against the live source page or document named in citation_url; citation_quote is copied from it. Chemicals were checked against the CIB&RC 'List of pesticides which are banned, refused registration and restricted in use' (updated 31.07.2026). Whether each product's label claim includes mango was NOT verified: the user must check the product label.

Anthracnose.title: Pseudomonas fluorescens spray on flowers and fruit bunches
Anthracnose.application_guidance: Spray flowers and bunches at 3-week intervals from October; 5 to 7 sprays in total.
Anthracnose.citation_source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Mango, Anthracnose
Anthracnose.citation_quote: Foliar spray of P. fluorescens (FP 7) @ 5g/like on flower branches at 3 weeks interval from October onwards. 5-7 sprays one to be given on flowers and bunches.

Anthracnose.title: Copper oxychloride spray for leaf infection
Anthracnose.application_guidance: Collect and burn diseased leaves, twigs and fruits first. Then spray the foliage.
Anthracnose.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Anthracnose.citation_quote: The foliar infection can be controlled by spraying of copper oxychloride (0.3%)

Anthracnose.title: Carbendazim spray for blossom infection
Anthracnose.application_guidance: Spray at 15-day intervals during flowering. For pre-harvest sprays, the last spray must fall 15 days before harvest.
Anthracnose.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Anthracnose.citation_quote: Blossom infection can be controlled effectively by spraying of Bavistin (0.1%) at 15 days interval. ... Pre-harvest sprays of hexaconazole (0.01%) or Carbendazim (0.1%) at 15 days interval should be done in such a way that the last spray falls 15 days prior to harvest.

Bacterial Canker.title: Sanitation and windbreaks
Bacterial Canker.application_guidance: Inspect the orchard regularly, remove infected parts, plant windbreaks to reduce wounding of leaves, and raise rootstock seedlings only from stones of healthy fruits.
Bacterial Canker.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Bacterial Canker.citation_quote: Regular inspection of orchards, sanitation and seedling certification are recommended as preventive measures. ... Use of wind-breaks helps in reducing brushing/ wounding and thus reduces chance of infection.

Bacterial Canker.title: Copper oxychloride spray in severe infection
Bacterial Canker.application_guidance: For severe infection. (The source also lists Streptocycline; it is not suggested here because a phase-out of streptomycin and tetracycline in agriculture has been ordered in draft. Check its current status with your agriculture officer.)
Bacterial Canker.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Bacterial Canker.citation_quote: In severe infection, spraying of Streptocycline (300 ppm) or copper oxychloride (0.3%) is more effective.

Powdery Mildew.title: Wettable sulphur spray at early panicle stage
Powdery Mildew.dosage_rate: 0.2% spray (2 g per litre of water)
Powdery Mildew.application_guidance: Spray when panicles are 3 to 4 inches long; a second application about 15 days later. Avoid spraying at full bloom.
Powdery Mildew.citation_source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Mango, Powdery mildew; National Horticulture Mission IPM Schedule for Mango Pests (2012)
Powdery Mildew.citation_quote: TNAU: "The first application may be soon after flowering, second 15 days later ... spray with Wettable sulphur (0.2%)". NHM: "Spray wettable sulphur (0.2%) when panicles are 3-4" in size. ... Spraying at full bloom needs to be avoided."

Sooty Mold.title: Control the honeydew insects, then spray starch
Sooty Mold.dosage_rate: Boil 1 kg starch or maida in 5 litres of water, then dilute to 20 litres
Sooty Mold.application_guidance: First control the insects whose honeydew feeds the mould (hoppers, scales, mealybugs). Then spray the starch; it dries into flakes that fall off with the mould. (The NHM bulletin gives a 2% starch spray.)
Sooty Mold.citation_source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Mango, Sooty mould
Sooty Mold.citation_quote: Management should be done for insects and sooty moulds simultaneously ... spray starch (1kg starch or maida boiled in 5 litres of water and diluted to 20 litres).

Fruit Fly.title: Destroy fallen fruit and plough in summer
Fruit Fly.application_guidance: Collect fallen infested fruits and bury them in a pit. Plough in summer to expose the pupae.
Fruit Fly.citation_source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Mango, Fruit fly
Fruit Fly.citation_quote: Collect fallen infested fruits and dispose them by dumping in a pit. Provide summer ploughing to expose the pupa.

Fruit Fly.title: Methyl eugenol lure traps
Fruit Fly.application_guidance: Hang traps during the fruiting period (April to August in the source), tied 3 to 5 feet above the ground. The source's trap mixture uses malathion, which is banned for use on mango in India (S.O. 4294(E), 3 Oct 2023): use only a trap insecticide whose label allows this use.
Fruit Fly.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Fruit Fly.citation_quote: Hanging of methyl eugenol wooden block traps soaked in ethanol, methyl eugenol and malathion (6:4:1) during fruiting period from April to August @10 traps/ ha tie them tightly at 3-5 feet above ground level.

Mealy Bug.title: Polythene trunk banding
Mealy Bug.product_name: Polythene sheet, 400 gauge, 20 cm wide, with fruit-tree grease
Mealy Bug.dosage_rate: One band per tree, 50 cm above the ground
Mealy Bug.application_guidance: Band the trunk in the middle of December, below the junction of the branches. Tie with jute thread and smear grease on the lower edge of the band so the nymphs cannot climb.
Mealy Bug.citation_source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Mango, Giant mealybug
Mealy Bug.citation_quote: Band the trees with 20 cm wide alkalthene of polythene (400 gauge) in the middle of December ... 50 cm above ground level.

Mealy Bug.title: Release of the Australian ladybird beetle
Mealy Bug.citation_source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Mango, Giant mealybug
Mealy Bug.citation_quote: Release of Australian ladybird beetle, Cryptolaemus montrouzieri @ 10/tree.

Scale Insect.title: Prune infested parts and remove attendant ants
Scale Insect.application_guidance: Prune heavily infested branches to open the canopy and destroy them immediately. Removing the ants that tend the scales lets natural enemies control them. (The chemicals named in the sources, phosphamidon and dimethoate, are banned or restricted for mango in India and are not suggested.)
Scale Insect.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal; TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Mango, Scales
Scale Insect.citation_quote: Prune heavily infested plant parts to open the tree canopy and destroy them immediately. ... Removal of attendant ants may permit natural enemies to control the insect.

Mango Hopper.title: Neem (azadirachtin) spray at the start of hopper build-up
Mango Hopper.application_guidance: Spray at the initial stage of the hopper population. Keep the canopy open by pruning overcrowded branches after the rainy season.
Mango Hopper.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Mango Hopper.citation_quote: Spraying of 0.2% Nimbicidin or Azadirachtin 3000 ppm@2m/l at initial stage of hopper population.

Mango Hopper.title: Imidacloprid spray at panicle stages (need-based)
Mango Hopper.application_guidance: Only if there are more than 5-10 hoppers per panicle: first spray early in panicle formation, second at full panicle length, third after fruit set (pea size). Minimise chemical sprays and rotate insecticides.
Mango Hopper.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Mango Hopper.citation_quote: Spray Lambda cyhalothrin 5% EC@ 0.5 ml or imidacloprid 200 SL @ 0.25 ml/l ... First spray should be done at early stage of panicle formation if hopper population, is more than 5-10 panicle, second spray at full length stage of panicle and the third spray after fruit setting (at pea size).

Stem Borer.title: Remove infested branches and plug the bore holes
Stem Borer.product_name: Kerosene- or petrol-soaked cotton, mud plug
Stem Borer.dosage_rate: One soaked cotton plug per hole
Stem Borer.application_guidance: Cut and destroy affected branches with grubs and pupae. Clean each hole, insert cotton wool soaked in kerosene or petrol and plug it with mud. (The source also lists dichlorvos, which is banned in India and is not suggested.)
Stem Borer.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Stem Borer.citation_quote: Cut and destroy affected branches with grubs and pupae. Clean hole and insert cotton wool soaked in emulsion of dichlorvos (0.05%) or kerosene or petrol in each hole and plug them with mud.

Stem Borer.title: Entomopathogenic fungi
Stem Borer.product_name: Metarhizium anisopliae or Beauveria bassiana formulation
Stem Borer.application_guidance: Use as directed on the product label.
Stem Borer.citation_source: National Horticulture Mission, IPM Schedule for Mango Pests, Extension Bulletin No. 1 (2012), hosted on the TNAU Agritech Portal
Stem Borer.citation_quote: Use of green muscardine fungi, Metarhizium anisopliae or Beauveria bassianna.
